cards.text: Out in the wilderness, Miriam and Aaron, Moses' sister and brother (Numbers 26:59), start criticizing Moses. Family, friend. NOBODY knows where to aim like family.

cards.question: Miriam and Aaron are criticizing their brother Moses. What's it about?

answers.text: The way he led them out

cards.text: Then the two of them say out loud what's on their minds. And it's all about who the LORD talks through.

cards.question: What are Miriam and Aaron saying about the LORD?

answers.text: He has stopped speaking at all
He only speaks through the elders

cards.question: True or false: Miriam and Aaron's complaint about Moses stays just between the two of them.

cards.text: The LORD heard them, friend. That's finding out the boss was in the group chat the WHOLE time.

cards.question: Right here the passage stops to tell us something about Moses himself. What does it say?

answers.text: He was the most humble man on earth
He was the bravest man on earth
He was the wisest man on earth

cards.text: The most humble man on earth. And here I am bragging to the oven every time a stamp comes out clean. Then suddenly the LORD tells all three of them to come out.

cards.question: Where does the LORD tell Moses, Aaron and Miriam to come out to?

cards.text: So the three go out, and the LORD comes down in a pillar of cloud and stands at the entrance to the Tent. Then He calls two of them forward.

cards.question: Which two does the LORD call forward at the entrance to the Tent?

cards.text: Aaron and Miriam step forward, and nobody gets called up front by name for good news. Then the LORD says if there's a prophet among them, He'll reveal Himself in a vision and speak in a dream.

cards.question: Then the LORD talks about His servant Moses. True or false: He says Moses is faithful in all His house.
A prophet gets visions and dreams. How does the LORD say He speaks with Moses?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks them, "Why then were you unafraid to speak against My servant Moses?" That's not a question you answer, friend. That's one you just stand there and FEEL.

cards.question: Before the LORD departs from the Tent, what happens toward Miriam and Aaron?

answers.text: He thanks them for speaking up
He lets the whole thing go

cards.text: As the cloud lifts from above the Tent, suddenly Miriam is leprous, white as snow. Aaron turns toward her and sees it.

cards.question: Aaron sees that Miriam is leprous. Who does he turn to and plead with?
Aaron begs Moses not to hold against them the ___ they so foolishly committed.

cards.text: Then Aaron pleads for Miriam. Please, he says, don't let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed.

cards.question: Aaron is pleading with Moses, the same brother Miriam just criticized. What does Moses do?

answers.text: Cries out to God to heal her
Sends her out of the camp himself
Asks the elders to decide for him

cards.text: Five words from Moses: "O God, please heal her!" No speech, no told-you-so. Then the LORD answers with a question: if her father had only spit in her face, wouldn't she be in disgrace?

cards.question: How long does the LORD say Miriam must be confined outside the camp?
True or false: The LORD says that after her seven days outside the camp, Miriam may be brought back in.
While Miriam is confined outside the camp for seven days, the people ___ until she is brought in again.

cards.text: After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camp in the Wilderness of Paran. And Miriam goes with them.

findings.problem: Moses appears for the first time in the passage on this card but is never introduced. Miriam and Aaron are explained only in relation to him ('Moses' sister and brother'), and the card never says who Moses is, such as Israel's leader.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He thanks them for speaking up' is not believable. The previous card has just shown the LORD rebuking them ('Why then were you unafraid to speak against My servant Moses?'), so no thoughtful baker would consider it, and it reads as a throwaway option.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Who does he turn to and plead with?' with Moses as the answer. In Numbers 12:10 Aaron turns toward Miriam, not Moses. He then speaks to Moses (12:11). The question says something the text shows is wrong, and it contradicts card 1 ('Aaron turns toward her').

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Only the right answer fits the sentence. A 'sin' is something you commit. 'Debt' and 'vow' don't work with 'so foolishly committed,' so grammar alone gives away the answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Sends her out of the camp himself' can be argued. Miriam is confined outside the camp in this passage (12:14-15), and the text never says who confines her, so a baker could argue that Moses, as leader, sent her out.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The story cards in stop 2 are mostly plain retelling with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Cards 1, 4 and 10 are straight summaries, and card 6's 'No speech, no told-you-so' is the only touch of personality in the stop.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
